info.title: LogB
info.description:
The HTTP API behind LogB, served under `/api`.

Two credentials work everywhere except token management: the `logb_session` cookie a browser gets from `POST /auth/login`, and an `Authorization: Bearer logb_pat_...` token for clients that are not browsers. A client obtains its first token by logging in interactively once and calling `POST /auth/tokens`; token management deliberately refuses bearer credentials, so a leaked token cannot mint replacements.

**Writing offline.** `POST /objects/{id}/activities` and `POST /objects/{id}/attachments` accept a `client_op_id`: any string unique to the write, generated once by the client and kept across every retry. The server records it under a unique index, so replaying a write whose response was lost resolves to the row already created instead of duplicating it. Any client that queues writes while offline should use it.

This document is checked against the running router by `tests/openapi.rs`: a route added, removed or renamed without updating it fails the build.

get.summary: Liveness probe. The only route needing no credential.
Whether the instance still needs its first (admin) user.

post.summary: Create the first user. Refused once any user exists.
Exchange credentials for a session cookie. Rate limited per IP.
End every session of this account, this one included.

get.summary: The signed-in user.
List this user's API tokens. Never includes the token itself.

post.summary: Issue an API token. The plaintext is in this response and nowhere else, ever: only a hash is stored. Requires a session cookie, never a bearer token.

delete.summary: Revoke a token. Takes effect on its next request.

get.summary: Objects owned by this user, one level of the tree at a time: top-level objects by default, one object's direct children with `parent_id`, or every object the user owns regardless of nesting with `all=true`. `archived` selects which half of the tree is listed either way.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: False (the default) lists live objects, true lists archived ones. The two sets are disjoint; there is no value that returns both.

parameters.name: parent_id
parameters.description: Omitted (or null) lists top-level objects only -- those with no parent, which is what the dashboard asks for. An id lists that object's direct children, one level deep, not its whole subtree. Ignored when `all` is true.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Every object the user owns, at every depth, still filtered by `archived`. Overrides `parent_id`. This is what a client that builds the tree itself -- or that must not silently lose nested objects -- should send.

200.description: Already created: the row this `client_uuid` names

409.description: `client_uuid` (or `client_op_id`) names a row the caller cannot reuse

get.summary: One object.

patch.summary: Replace an object. Every field except `cover_attachment_id` is a full replace: a field left out is written as null, so send the object whole. `cover_attachment_id` is three-state — absent keeps the cover, null clears it, an id sets it.

delete.summary: Delete an object with its activities, reminders and attachments. The files and blobs they referenced deliberately survive until the retention purge.

get.summary: Cost and consumption rollups for one object.

parameters.name: contents
parameters.description: Include every non-deleted descendant in by_year, by_category, by_month and ownership. Counter and fuel figures always stay the object's own.

get.summary: How fast one object's counter rises -- the rate alone, without the cost rollups of /insights.

counter_per_day_milli.description: Counter units per day, x1000, as in Insights.counter_per_day_milli; null without enough history

get.summary: Up to 20 recent, distinct activity titles for this object, for repeat suggestions.
One page of the object's timeline, newest first. `X-Total-Count` carries the unpaged total. `limit` is clamped to 500 rather than refused.

X-Total-Count.description: Matching rows in total, ignoring the page window

post.summary: Log an activity. Send `client_op_id` to make a retry idempotent.

200.description: Already created: the row this `client_op_id` or `client_uuid` names

409.description: `client_uuid` (or `client_op_id`) names a row the caller cannot reuse

get.summary: One activity, with its attachments.

patch.summary: Replace an activity. A full replace, as with objects.

delete.summary: Delete an activity and its attachments.

get.summary: Files attached to this object.

post.summary: Upload a file, optionally onto one activity. Identical bytes are stored once and shared. Send `client_op_id` to make a retry idempotent.

client_uuid.description: Identity the client minted before the server saw the row. A second create carrying the same value answers 200 with the row the first one made; one naming another account's row, another object's row, or a tombstone answers 409. Only the shape is checked, never a UUID grammar.

200.description: Already stored: the row this `client_op_id` or `client_uuid` names

409.description: `client_uuid` (or `client_op_id`) names a row the caller cannot reuse

delete.summary: Detach a file. The stored bytes are reclaimed once nothing references them and the tombstone has aged out of the sync window.

get.summary: The original bytes. Served from this origin under a sandbox policy; only a short list of types renders in place, everything else downloads.
A thumbnail, for image attachments.
Reminders for one object.

post.summary: Create a reminder, due on a date, a counter reading, or both.

200.description: Already created: the row this `client_uuid` names

409.description: `client_uuid` (or `client_op_id`) names a row the caller cannot reuse

get.summary: Everything due now, plus anything coming due within `within_days`. A snoozed reminder appears in neither until its snooze lapses.
One reminder.

post.summary: Mark done, optionally against the activity that did it. A repeating reminder schedules its successor from that point.
Suppress a reminder for `days`, without touching its real due date.

delete.summary: Clear a snooze, making the reminder due again immediately.

get.summary: Objects (by name and description) and activities (by title and notes) matching `q`. An object's `type` is an identifier, not searchable text.
Spend across all of the caller's objects: over time, by object (children rolled up), by type and by category.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Restrict to one year; over_time then has twelve YYYY-MM buckets. Omitted: all years, one YYYY bucket each.

parameters.name: purchases
parameters.description: Count objects' purchase prices, as by_category bucket purchase_price. Skipped for an object with a costed purchase entry.

400.description: year is not a number or outside 0..=9999

get.summary: Instance settings.
Where the caller's daily digest goes, and what a browser needs to subscribe to push.

put.summary: Set the caller's own digest webhook and its format.

post.summary: Send a test notification now to the caller's own webhook and every browser they subscribed.
Subscribe a browser to push notifications. An endpoint already known moves to the caller.

delete.summary: Unsubscribe one of the caller's browsers. Idempotent.

get.summary: Everything this user owns as a zip: JSON plus the original files. Streamed.

post.summary: Restore an export. Adds to what is there; it does not replace it.

get.summary: Every user. Admin only.

patch.summary: Change a user's password or language. Anyone may change their own; only an admin may change anyone else's. A password change ends every session AND revokes every API token of that account.

delete.summary: Delete a user with everything they own. Admin only.

post.summary: Apply a batch of offline ops with field-level last-write-wins.
post.description: Every op in the batch is applied inside one transaction, so a client that retries after a lost response finds either all of its ops recorded or none. `results` is positional: `results[i]` describes `ops[i]`. An op that loses the last-write-wins comparison is `superseded` -- recorded in the change feed, but not written to the row; only a malformed or unauthorised op is `rejected`. Replaying a `client_op_id` already in the log reports `accepted` without applying it a second time.

get.summary: Page through the change feed from a cursor.
get.description: `since` is the `next_seq` from the previous call, or 0 for a first pull. `complete` is false when the page filled exactly, meaning the client should pull again immediately with the returned `next_seq`. A `since` older than the server's retention horizon -- including a non-zero `since` against a log that has been purged empty -- answers 410 instead of a silently-incomplete 200; the client must re-bootstrap from a fresh export rather than trust an incremental catch-up. A non-zero `since` also requires `epoch` to match the database's current one -- see the `epoch` parameter -- or the same 410 is returned.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: The cursor to resume after: the `next_seq` from a previous pull, or 0 for a first pull.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of changes to return. Clamped to [1, 1000].

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The `epoch` from a previous pull or bootstrap, proving which database `since` was issued against. Required whenever `since` is non-zero; a mismatched or missing epoch answers 410, the same as a stale `since`, because a restored database reissues `changes.seq` for entirely different ops.

410.description: `since` predates the retained history; re-bootstrap instead of resuming.

get.summary: The full snapshot a new device starts from, or that a stale device falls back to.
get.description: Every live (non-tombstoned) row the caller owns, across every syncable table, plus `seq` -- the cursor to resume incremental pulls from -- and `server_time`. `seq` is read before the rows are, so an op landing between the two reads is, at worst, delivered again by the first `GET /sync/pull`; the apply path is idempotent, so that is harmless. This is the only read path that returns `client_uuid` for existing rows, so a device must bootstrap before it can push anything that references them. Used both by a brand-new device and by one whose cursor is older than the retention horizon, after `GET /sync/pull` answers 410.

get.summary: Which database this instance is serving, and whether it may be changed from here. Admin only.
get.description: Never carries a credential: the user, password and query string of the connection URL are removed before anything is reported. `pointer_writable` is false when `LOGB_DATABASE_URL` is set -- the environment always wins over the choice made here -- or when the data directory will not take the pointer file. `pending` is set once a switch has happened and the restart has not.

get.summary: Whether LogB is taking automatic backups of the database it is serving, and where. Admin only.
get.description: `not_ours` on PostgreSQL: LogB is not the thing that backs this database up there, regardless of whether `LOGB_BACKUP_DIR` happens to be set -- it may well be, left over from a compose file, on an instance that was migrated through Settings. `off` is SQLite with no `LOGB_BACKUP_DIR` configured. `scheduled` is SQLite with one configured, and carries the directory, the hour it runs at, and the newest snapshot's timestamp -- `null` when the directory has no snapshot yet, including one that does not exist at all before the first run.

post.summary: Look at another database without changing it. Admin only.
post.description: Opens one connection, reads the server version and whether the database already holds LogB data, and closes it. No schema is created and nothing is written, so a URL typed by mistake is not turned into a LogB database. An unreachable destination is a 200 with `reachable: false`, not an error: not being able to connect is the answer to the question, and the reason is scrubbed of anything the URL carried.

post.summary: Copy this instance's database into another one and remember the choice. Admin only.
post.description:
Copies every table, row for row and id for id, from inside the write transaction every write in this application goes through: no write can land on the source while it runs, so the copy is taken from one point in time. **The request therefore blocks for the whole copy** -- seconds to minutes, depending on the database -- and reads go on being served throughout. A client should allow for that rather than timing out.

The pointer file is written only if the copy succeeded, so a failure leaves the instance exactly where it was. Nothing moves until the process restarts: see `POST /database/restart`. Blobs under the data directory are not copied -- they are content-addressed files and pair with any database.

Refused with 400 when `LOGB_DATABASE_URL` is set (the environment decides instead), when the destination is the database already in use, or when the destination cannot be copied onto. Every message is scrubbed of the URL's credentials.

200.description: The copy finished and the choice was remembered

400.description: No URL, the database already in use, the environment deciding instead, or a destination that cannot be copied onto

503.description: The copy finished but the choice could not be remembered

post.summary: Exit the process, so the next start opens the database that was chosen. Admin only.
post.description: Answers 202 and then exits, a moment later, once the response has been written. There is no way to swap the connection pool underneath a running instance, so a restart is the whole mechanism -- and LogB does not start itself again: something has to supervise the process (systemd, a container restart policy). If nothing does, the instance stays down until it is started by hand.

bearerToken.description: An API token from `POST /auth/tokens`. Does not expire; revoke it to end it.

timezone.description: Setup only: the browser's IANA timezone, stored as the instance's unless `LOGB_TIMEZONE` is set. Ignored when it does not parse

prefix.description: The first characters of the token, for recognition only

last_used_at.description: Recorded at most once a day

token.description: The plaintext, readable only in this response

Category.description: `reading` is an entry that records nothing but a counter value, and requires `counter_value`

Ancestor.description: One link in an object's ancestor chain, as a breadcrumb needs it.

parent_id.description: The object this one sits inside -- a garage inside a house -- or null for a top-level object.

ancestors.description: Root first, nearest ancestor last, this object excluded. Filled in only by the single-object responses (GET/POST/PATCH of one object); `GET /objects` always returns it empty, since no list view draws a breadcrumb and filling it would cost one recursive query per row.

client_uuid.description: The row's sync identity: what a sync op names it by, and what `client_uuid` on a create set it to. Null only for a row that predates the sync tables and has not been backfilled, which no shipped migration leaves behind.

last_reading_date.description: The newest entry with a counter value

parent_id.description: Three-state on PATCH: omit the field to keep the current parent, send null to make the object top-level again, send an id to move it. On POST, omitted and null both mean top-level. The id must name one of your own undeleted objects, and must be neither this object nor one of its descendants, or the request is refused with 400.

client_uuid.description: Identity the client minted before the server saw the row. A second create carrying the same value answers 200 with the row the first one made; one naming another account's row, another object's row, or a tombstone answers 409. Only the shape is checked, never a UUID grammar.

cost_cents.description: Money is always integer cents; never a float

quantity_milli.description: Fuel quantity in thousandths of `fuel_unit`; fuel activities only

client_uuid.description: The row's sync identity: what a sync op names it by, and what `client_uuid` on a create set it to. Null only for a row that predates the sync tables and has not been backfilled, which no shipped migration leaves behind.

client_op_id.description: Generated once per write and kept across retries; makes a replay idempotent

edited_at.description: PATCH only: when an edit was made, for one sent later (queued offline). Each field it changes is kept only if nothing changed that field after this moment. Capped at the server's now

client_uuid.description: Identity the client minted before the server saw the row. A second create carrying the same value answers 200 with the row the first one made; one naming another account's row, another object's row, or a tombstone answers 409. Only the shape is checked, never a UUID grammar.

The row's sync identity: what a sync op names it by, and what `client_uuid` on a create set it to. Null only for a row that predates the sync tables and has not been backfilled, which no shipped migration leaves behind.

file_uuid.description: The sync identity of the file row this attachment references. Two attachments of identical bytes share one.

due.description: Due now, accounting for any live snooze

days_until.description: Against the real due date, snooze or not

kind.description: `service` watches due_date/due_counter and is marked done. `reading` wants a counter reading every `every_n` `every_unit`s, counted from the newest reading and never before `due_date` (its start); logging any activity with a counter value satisfies it, and it cannot be marked done

last_reading_date.description: Date of the object's newest counter reading on or before today

next_due_date.description: When it comes due by date: `due_date` for a service reminder, derived for a reading reminder. `days_until` is measured to this

estimated_due_date.description: For a service reminder with an unreached due_counter: when recent usage projects the counter to reach it. Feeds the `within_days` lookahead; never makes a reminder due

client_uuid.description: The row's sync identity: what a sync op names it by, and what `client_uuid` on a create set it to. Null only for a row that predates the sync tables and has not been backfilled, which no shipped migration leaves behind.

kind.description: Fixed at create; a PATCH naming another kind is refused. A reading reminder takes every_n and every_unit, needs an object with a counter, refuses due_counter and repeat_*, and treats a missing due_date as today

client_uuid.description: Identity the client minted before the server saw the row. A second create carrying the same value answers 200 with the row the first one made; one naming another account's row, another object's row, or a tombstone answers 409. Only the shape is checked, never a UUID grammar.

fills.description: Consumption per fill for up to the twelve newest fills, oldest first

counter_per_day_milli.description: Counter units per day, x1000, from the earliest reading in the last 180 days (or of all, when that span is under 14 days) to the newest; null without enough history

usage_by_month.description: The last twelve calendar months, oldest first; empty without a counter or a measurable month

amount.description: Null when no reading in the month, or none before it to measure from

has_contents.description: Whether the object has any non-deleted child

purchase_cents.description: Purchase prices counted; an object with a costed purchase entry contributes 0

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD: purchase date, else creation date

per_year_cents.description: total_cents per 365 days owned, until the archive date or today; null under 90 days

by_month.description: Twelve calendar months ending with the current one, oldest first, zeros included

years.description: Every year with spend, newest first; ignores the year filter.

ObjectHit.description: An object as `/search` returns it: the stored columns plus the parent's name, so a list of four things called "Filter" says which object each one lives in. Deliberately not an `Object` -- it carries no `stats`, `cover_file_id` or `ancestors`, none of which the search computes.

parent_name.description: The name of the object this one sits inside, or null for a top-level object.

ActivityHit.description: An activity as `/search` returns it: a subset of `Activity`'s columns plus the owning object's name. It carries no `quantity_milli`, `client_op_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` or `attachments`; fetch the activity itself for those.

cost_cents.description: Money is always integer cents; never a float

timezone.description: The instance's IANA timezone: which day a due date is read against, and when the daily digest goes out. First-run setup stores the browser's; `LOGB_TIMEZONE` overrides both

timezone_locked.description: True when `LOGB_TIMEZONE` decides the timezone; a PUT naming another one is refused

client_op_id.description: Unique per op; replaying one is a no-op.

field.description: Required for `set`; must be a syncable column of `entity`.

value.description: The new value for `set`. Its shape must match the target column: a string for a text column, an integer for an integer column, or null to clear it -- a boolean is rejected everywhere, and any other mismatch (e.g. a string into an integer column) comes back `rejected` rather than being coerced.

edited_at.description: RFC3339. Canonicalised to UTC milliseconds before it is compared.

device_id.description: Breaks ties on equal `edited_at`; the greater string wins.

results.description: One entry per op, in the order the ops were sent.

ids.description: client_uuid to the server's integer id, for references a client only knows by uuid.

seq.description: The monotonic pull cursor. Pass the last row's `seq` back as `since` to resume.

field.description: Null for `create` and `delete`; only a `set` names a field.

value.description: Double-encoded JSON: this string is itself the JSON-serialized form of the value that was set, so a string value arrives as e.g. `"\"Golf VII\""` and a client must `JSON.parse` it to recover the real value. Null here is ambiguous by construction: an explicit `value: null` on a `set` (clearing the field) is stored as SQL NULL and is indistinguishable from a `create`/`delete` row, which never carries a value at all. A field cleared through a REST write (a PATCH sending null, or a delete cascade unlinking a reference) is stored as the double-encoded JSON null -- the four-character string "null" -- rather than SQL NULL, so a client must treat both as "clear".

entity_id.description: The server's integer id for `entity_uuid`: what REST responses and `/files/{id}` use. Null once retention has hard-purged the row.

next_seq.description: Pass as `since` on the next call.

complete.description: False when the page filled exactly; the client should pull again immediately.

epoch.description: Which database these seq numbers belong to. A client stores it beside its cursor and passes it back as the `epoch` query parameter on its next pull.

objects.description: Every live row from `objects`, verbatim, keyed by column name.

activities.description: Every live row from `activities` whose object is also live.

reminders.description: Every live row from `reminders` whose object is also live.

attachments.description: Every live row from `attachments` whose object is also live.

files.description: Every live row from `files`, verbatim, keyed by column name.

seq.description: Pass as `since` on the first `GET /sync/pull` call.

epoch.description: Which database this snapshot came from. Pass alongside `seq` as the `epoch` query parameter on the first `GET /sync/pull` call.

DatabaseLocation.description: A database with nothing secret in it: no user, no password, no query string.

host.description: host:port for PostgreSQL; null for SQLite, which has no host

database.description: The database name for PostgreSQL, the file for SQLite

pointer_writable.description: Whether the database may be chosen from here at all

pending.description: The database a restart would move onto, once a switch has happened

version.description: What the server says it is, or null when there was nothing to ask

message.description: Why, when that is worth saying. Never carries the URL's credentials.

directory.description: The configured backup directory. null for off and not_ours

last_at.description: The newest snapshot's timestamp, or null when there isn't one yet

hour.description: The hour backups run at. null for off and not_ours

epoch.description: The identity the destination now advertises; every synced device re-bootstraps against it

pointer.description: The file the choice was remembered in

restart_required.description: Always true: this instance is still serving the database it started on

timezone.description: Optional IANA name. Refused when it is not one, or when `LOGB_TIMEZONE` sets a different one

url.description: This user's own digest webhook. Null keeps them in the instance digest

push_devices.description: Browsers this user has turned push notifications on in

vapid_public_key.description: `applicationServerKey` for PushManager.subscribe: an uncompressed P-256 point, base64url

hour.description: The hour, in the instance timezone, the digest goes out

url.description: An http(s) URL; blank or null for none

webhook.description: `sent`, why it failed, or null without a webhook of this user's own

PushSubscription.description: What PushSubscription.toJSON() produces. The endpoint must be https
